info.title: PrescribeRx REST API
info.description:
REST API for the PrescribeRx telehealth and pharmacy platform.

## Required Headers

Every request to `/api/v1/*` MUST include these headers:

```
Accept: application/json
Authorization: Bearer {token}       (all endpoints except /auth/login and /auth/password/forgot)
Content-Type: application/json      (POST/PUT/PATCH requests with a JSON body)
```

**The `Accept: application/json` header is mandatory.** Without it, authentication
failures historically returned a 302 redirect to the web login page instead of a
JSON 401 body — masking the real error from integrators. The server now injects
this header via middleware on every `/api/*` request as a safety net, but clients
SHOULD still send it explicitly for portability and to match the documented contract.

If you ever receive an HTML response or a 302 redirect, check that (1) your HTTP
client is actually sending the `Accept: application/json` header, and (2) the full
token string from `POST /auth/login` is in the `Authorization` header (including
the `{id}|` prefix Sanctum emits).

## Authentication

All authenticated endpoints require a Bearer token obtained via `POST /auth/login`.

```
Authorization: Bearer {token}
```

Tokens are scoped with abilities based on user type. The ability list
below mirrors `App\Enums\Api\TokenAbility::forUserType()` exactly — that
method is the authoritative source. Wildcards are NOT issued (e.g.,
`encounter:*`); each ability is granted explicitly.

| User Type           | Value | Abilities |
|---------------------|-------|-----------|
| Provider            | 0     | encounter:read, encounter:create, encounter:update, prescription:read, prescription:create, prescription:sign, patient:read, patient:update, provider:read, provider:update, product:read |
| Patient             | 1     | patient:read, patient:update, patient:vitals, order:read, telehealth:read, telehealth:submit, encounter:read, prescription:read, product:read |
| Sales Organization  | 2     | sales-org:read, sales-org:update, client:read, client:create, order:read, order:create, order:update, product:read, patient:read, patient:create, patient:update, prescription:read, telehealth:read, telehealth:submit, encounter:read, encounter:create, encounter:update, webhook:read, webhook:create, webhook:update, webhook:delete |
| API                 | 3     | `*` (all abilities) |
| System Admin        | 4     | `*` (all abilities) |
| Client              | 6     | client:read, client:update, order:create, order:read, order:update, prescription:read, patient:read, patient:create, patient:update, product:read, telehealth:read, telehealth:submit, encounter:read, encounter:create, encounter:update, webhook:read, webhook:create, webhook:update, webhook:delete |
| Super Admin         | 8     | `*` (all abilities) |
| Client Provider     | 9     | client:read, client:update, order:create, order:read, order:update, prescription:read, prescription:create, prescription:sign, encounter:create, encounter:read, encounter:update, patient:read, patient:create, patient:update, product:read, provider:read, provider:update, telehealth:read, telehealth:submit, webhook:read, webhook:create, webhook:update, webhook:delete |
| Client Administrator| 10    | Identical ability list to Client (tenant-scoped at policy layer) |

Ambassador (5), Affiliate (7), and Telehealth Admin (11) currently
receive no API abilities — `forUserType()` returns `[]` for them.

**Token type guard on payment.mode=authorize:** sales-org / client tokens
cannot use `payment.mode=authorize` on the unified intake endpoint —
PRX is not the merchant of record for API-driven flows. Use
`reference_captured` (record-only) or `patient_review` (deferred portal
pay) instead. Embed-form tokens (browser-served) DO support `authorize`
because PRX is the merchant on the embed flow.

## Response Format

All responses follow a standard envelope:

```json
{
  "success": true,
  "data": { ... },
  "message": "Optional message",
  "meta": {
    "request_id": "uuid",
    "timestamp": "2026-04-03T12:00:00+00:00"
  }
}
```

Paginated responses include `meta.pagination`:

```json
{
  "meta": {
    "pagination": {
      "current_page": 1,
      "last_page": 5,
      "per_page": 25,
      "total": 112,
      "from": 1,
      "to": 25
    }
  }
}
```

## Rate Limiting

| Scope | Limit |
|-------|-------|
| General | 60 requests/minute per user |
| Auth endpoints | 10 requests/minute per IP |
| Order creation | 30 requests/minute per user |

Rate limit headers: `X-RateLimit-Limit`, `X-RateLimit-Remaining`, `Retry-After` (on 429).

## HTTP Status Codes

| Code | Meaning |
|------|---------|
| 200 | Success |
| 201 | Created |
| 400 | Business rule error |
| 401 | Unauthenticated |
| 402 | Payment failed |
| 403 | Forbidden |
| 404 | Not found |
| 422 | Validation error |
| 429 | Rate limited |
| 500 | Server error |

tags.description:
Surface for 3rd-party telehealth companies that prescribe in their
own e-Rx system and route fulfillment through PrescribeRx. Three
endpoints: register providers by NPI, look them up after admin
approval, and submit fully-formed orders with the signed PDF
attached. Sales-org tokens (multi-clinic integrators) AND client
tokens (single-clinic direct integrators) are both supported —
the effective sales-org id resolves from `user.sales_organization_id`
or `user.client.sales_organization_id`. The three abilities
(`external-telehealth:providers:write`/`:read`/`orders:write`) are
NOT in any default ability set — granted manually per integrator.
Reference guide: `/api/docs/external-telehealth-guide`.

directly because the public contract is the JS widget — adding

consistency win. Treat the response shapes as the authoritative
contract.

tags.name: Peptides
tags.description:
Read-only Peptide / Ingredient Knowledge Base — a global catalog of
active compounds with narrative sections (overview, pharmacology,
clinical evidence, dosing guidelines, safety profile, patient summary),
approved dosing guidance, and clinical references.

**Audience shaping** — the `audience` query param (`patient` | `clinician`,
default `patient`) shapes the detail returned. `patient` returns the
overview + patient summary; `clinician` adds the dense clinical sections
(pharmacology, clinical evidence, dosing guidelines, safety profile,
mechanism, evidence score). Dosing guidance is returned to both.

**Clinical-safety gating** — approved drug-interactions and preclusions are
returned ONLY when `audience=clinician` AND the token holds the
`peptide:clinical:read` ability. A read-only token, or a patient-audience
request, receives those fields as `null` (gated, not empty).

**PRX prerequisites** — the `peptide:read` ability (and, for the safety
data, `peptide:clinical:read`) is granted MANUALLY per integrator on the
API token; neither is in any default ability set. Only `review_status`
= `approved` supporting data is ever exposed. No PHI; global (no tenant scope).

post.description:
Stateless preclusion evaluator that mirrors the embed's live-firing
logic. Submit an encounter type + answer set (and optionally a
patient chart) and get back every preclusion that would fire —
without creating an encounter or mutating any chart data.

**Identical evaluation as the embed.** Under the hood the endpoint
calls the same `PreclusionCheckService` methods (`evaluateFieldPreclusions`
+ `checkPreclusions`) that the front-end Livewire `StepRenderer`
invokes on every keystroke. If the embed fires a preclusion for an
input, this endpoint fires the same one. Guaranteed by shared logic.

**Encounter type:** Provide exactly one of `encounter_type_id` or
`encounter_type_slug`.

**Answers:** Object keyed by `EncounterField.slug` (the same keys
you'd send to `POST /telehealth/intake/unified`). Values may be
string / number / boolean / array (arrays for multiselect / checkbox).
Partial answer sets are fine — only fields you supply are evaluated.

**Patient chart (optional):** When `patient_chart_id` is provided,
terminology-based preclusions also fire against the chart's
allergies / medications / conditions. Omit for a new-patient
pre-validation use case.

**Use cases:**
  - Live front-end validation as the patient answers questions
  - Pre-flight check before `POST /telehealth/intake/unified` to
    warn the patient about contraindications
  - Server-side audit: verify your stored answers still wouldn't
    fire preclusions today (e.g., after a clinical rules update)

**Returns** each triggered preclusion with a `source` tag:
  - `field_config` — per-field `preclusion_config` JSON rule (v1/v2)
  - `encounter_type_rule` — global preclusion attached to the
    EncounterType / ProductClass / ProductType
  - `terminology` — chart-based rule (only when `patient_chart_id`
    is supplied)

Plus a `summary` block with counts by severity and a `has_hard_stop`
boolean for quick gating.

post.summary: Unified intake -- create patient + encounter + answers
post.description:
Single-call endpoint that creates a patient (or finds existing by email+DOB),
creates an encounter, and submits intake answers in one request.

**Required (Encounter Intake Safeguards, 2026-07-14):** `patient.first_name`,
`patient.last_name`, `patient.email`, `patient.date_of_birth`,
`patient.phone`, a **shipping address** (`patient.shipping_address` OR
`patient.address`) with `street`/`city`/`state`/`zip`, and — unless the
encounter type is a quick consult (`is_quick_consult: true`) — a
product/package/plan selection. Missing any → `422` with per-field
`errors`. A duplicate re-POST that changes existing patient data → `409`
(use the PATCH endpoints to correct). See the `UnifiedIntakeRequest`
schema and the `409`/`422` responses below.

**Ordering a product TYPE (not a specific SKU):** to let the provider
choose the concrete concentration/SKU at prescribe-time, send the type
inside `products[]` as `{"product_type_id": "..."}` or
`{"product_type_slug": "..."}` — **NOT** as a top-level field. A
top-level `product_type_id` is silently ignored (it is not part of this
request schema), which produces an encounter with nothing to prescribe.
A generic-type line lands an `is_generic_reference` line the provider's
prescribing panel renders as "type → pick dose → pick eligible SKU",
exactly like a package's generic item. **This selection is mandatory
even when the encounter type pins its own product catalog** — on this
API the catalog alone does NOT satisfy the requirement (only the
interactive embed/wizard flows treat it as pre-selected); omit a line on
a non-quick-consult type and you get the `422` above.

**Encounter type:** Specify by `encounter_type_id`, `encounter_type_slug`, or `encounter_type_name` (priority: id > slug > name).

**Organization:** Use `client_id`/`client_number` and `sales_org_id`/`sales_org_number`. Falls back to authenticated user's org.

**Answers:** Key by field slug from `GET /telehealth/encounter-types/{id}/schema`.

**Scheduling (video visits):** Two booking flows. (1) Include the optional
top-level `appointment` object here to book inline — the time maps onto the
encounter (sets `scheduled_at`, assigns the provider, provisions the video
room + join link), returned as `video_room`. (2) Omit `appointment`, then
create the time separately: `GET /scheduling/availability/slots` → `POST
/encounters/{id}/schedule` (which additionally supports auto-assign by
omitting the provider). A scheduled time is always stored in UTC; a naive
`scheduled_start` is interpreted in `patient_timezone`.

**Idempotency:** Optional `Idempotency-Key` request header. When
provided, the response body for the first successful call is
cached for 24h under `(tenant, key)`. Any subsequent call with
the SAME key + same tenant within that window returns the prior
response verbatim, plus headers:
  - `X-Idempotent-Replayed: true`
  - `X-Idempotent-Original-At: <ISO8601>`
No duplicate encounter is created on replay. Without the header
the endpoint behaves as before (every call creates a new
encounter). Recommended pattern: generate a UUID per logical
intake submission and include it in your retry envelope so
transient errors / double-fires don't create duplicates.

**Payment & transaction details (IMPORTANT — read before integrating):**
The `payment` block is **optional** and this endpoint will **never reject
an intake for lacking payment detail** — an encounter is always created
so your clinical workflow is never blocked. However, what you send (or
omit) has real downstream consequences:

- **Pass the transaction detail whenever you have it.** Use
  `mode=authorize` (we charge), or — if you ran the charge on your own
  gateway — `mode=reference_preauth` / `mode=reference_captured` with the
  gateway transaction id **and the `amount`**. The amount drives accurate
  **P&L / revenue reporting**, lets the charge be attributed to your sales
  org's merchant + this customer, and enables billing of any future
  subscription / refill / deferred capture on that same merchant
  relationship. Omitting transaction detail is like omitting the
  package/plan — the provider and the system then have no record of what
  the patient requested or paid.
- **Collected payment in person / out of band (no electronic record)?**
  Omit `payment`, or use `mode=prepaid` (records the bypass + reason). The
  intake is accepted and flagged external; reconciliation is on your side.
- **FAILSAFE — future billing requires a vaulted card.** When an intake
  arrives with no chargeable method on file, **no future auto-billing**
  (subscription rebill, refill charge, deferred capture) will proceed for
  that patient until they vault a card (on your merchant, or a system
  merchant if your org has none). The patient is prompted to add a card —
  we never silently charge and never silently fail. Plan your flow so the
  patient vaults a method before any recurring billing is expected.

post.summary: Attach a scheduled time to an existing encounter
post.description:
Books a time onto an already-created encounter — the "create the encounter first, query availability, then attach the time" flow. Create the encounter without an appointment (e.g. via `POST /telehealth/intake/unified` with no `appointment` block), query `GET /scheduling/availability/slots`, then POST the chosen time here.
Unlike posting a bare `POST /scheduling/appointments`, this maps the time onto the ENCOUNTER via the canonical scheduling primitive: it sets `scheduled_at`, books + links the companion appointment, assigns the provider (→ `SCHEDULED`), and provisions the video room — so the visit actually appears as a scheduled encounter (with `video_room` + persistent join link + reminders).
**Provider is optional.** Supply `provider_profile_id` to pin a specific provider, or omit it to let the platform auto-assign an eligible provider available at that slot.
**Time handling.** `scheduled_start` is ISO-8601: a value carrying an offset (or `Z`) is respected as-is; a naive `Y-m-d H:i:s` value is interpreted in `patient_timezone` (defaulting to the patient's resolved timezone). The time is always stored in UTC.

post.summary: Record an externally-executed reversal (refund or void)
post.description:
The reverse-direction mirror of `payment.mode=reference_captured`. Under the shared-merchant model YOU ran the refund/void on your gateway; this records it on PrescribeRx so the ledger and the order reflect it. PRX **never calls the gateway here.** It records the reversal (an external transaction), updates the original transaction's refunded/voided ledger, flips the order's `payment_status` (which fires the `order.refunded` / `order.voided` webhook), and **halts still-unshipped fulfillment on a full reversal** (a partial refund does not stop the shipment).

Idempotent — a reversal already recorded for the same original gateway transaction + type is returned unchanged (dedup). A refund exceeding the refundable balance is refused (`409`).

**Invariant:** there must be exactly ONE reversal initiator. If you record reversals here, do NOT also use PrescribeRx's own gateway-calling refund/void (admin console) on the same order, or the customer is double-refunded.

post.summary: Accept (approve + pay for) a provider-added item
post.description:
Approves the item and charges it as a **separate, consented** sale against
the patient's vaulted card — never collected from the base authorization,
never auto-charged. Requires the `patient:approve-charge` ability.

Send `acknowledged_total` equal to the item's `total_price`; a mismatch
returns `409` with the current server price so a stale page cannot silently
pay a changed amount. The item is marked approved (and becomes shippable)
**only on a successful charge** — no chargeable card returns `402` and the
item stays pending. Fires the `approval.accepted` webhook on success.

**PRX charges — the caller never does.** The delta is a single consented sale
PRX runs on the shared merchant against the patient's vaulted profile; an
external portal must NOT charge locally (that would double-charge). Charging
and ship-eligibility are one atomic decision inside PRX (APPROVED only on a
successful charge).

**This endpoint is NON-idempotent from the client's perspective — `402`,
`409`, and `502` are all TERMINAL, do not blindly retry.** `502` (UNCERTAIN)
means the money moved but bookkeeping failed; a naive retry-on-5xx would
re-charge (the gateway idempotency key only truly dedups Stripe/Square). Send
an **`Idempotency-Key`** header and PRX will replay the prior money-outcome
response (`X-Idempotent-Replayed: true`) instead of charging again; a
genuinely new attempt must use a new key.

post.summary: Cancel a bulk order (by patient identifiers)

post.description:
SYNCHRONOUS checkout that creates a real `Order` (process `BULK_TO_CLIENT`, shipped to the client) and CHARGES the card in-request (`should_charge=true`, `capture_mode=sale`). Requires `order:read` AND `order:create`. Lines use product **UUIDs** (not SKUs).

**PRX prerequisite:** the client must have a configured merchant account or the charge fails (402). If you pass `billing_address_id` together with `payment_method_id`, the billing address is synced to the gateway CIM before the charge to avoid an AVS decline — recommended.

payment_method_id.description: Vaulted method to charge. Omit only if the flow tolerates no payment.

post.summary: Create a patient encounter (intake + vault payment)
post.description:
Creates a full patient graph in one transaction — User + PatientChart (+addresses, allergies, conditions) + a VAULTED payment method + an Encounter (`status=PENDING_INTAKE`). It does NOT create an order or charge a card; the payment method is vaulted for later. Requires only a valid Sanctum token (tenant is enforced inside the action).

**PRX prerequisites:** (1) an active `EncounterType` must exist for the `product_type_id` (else 404); (2) a merchant account must exist on the instance or be passed as `payment.merchant_account_id` (else 500 "No merchant account configured"); (3) the patient must have a **billing** address among `patient.addresses` to vault the card. An existing patient (matched by email) is updated & reused, not duplicated.

client_id.description: Must match the token's tenant or be omitted (else 422).

sales_organization_id.description: Must match the token's tenant or be omitted (else 422).

email.description: Matched case-insensitively to an existing patient; a non-patient user → 404.

addresses.description: At least one required; a BILLING address is required to vault payment.

intake_answers.description: If non-empty, requires_patient_intake=false and intake is skipped.

merchant_account_id.description: Optional; if omitted, resolved by MerchantAssignmentService (none → 500).

token.description: Gateway tokenization payload (fields vary by gateway; all nullable).

404.description: Email belongs to a non-patient user, no EncounterType for the product type, or no billing address

200.description: Lookup result (data is null when no match)

encounter_id.description: Optionally link the vital to an encounter.

The `owner` block is required — the owner user is created (roles assigned by user type), linked to the org, and receives an account-setup invitation; the org's `owner_id` is set to that new user (any `owner_id` you send is ignored). Depending on the caller and business rules the org may be auto-approved (owner activated immediately) or left PENDING for admin approval.

parent_id.description: Defaults to the caller's org if omitted.

Messages on an encounter's provider↔patient conversation, ordered `created_at, id`. Access is by encounter ownership (assigned provider, the patient's chart, or the owning client/sales-org tree).

**Incremental poll:** pass `after` (a message id from a prior `meta.latest_cursor`, or an ISO-8601 timestamp) to get only messages newer than the cursor. Bearer tokens cannot authorize the realtime broadcast channel, so POLL this endpoint: first call without `after`, then feed `meta.latest_cursor` back each time. The response `meta` here is `{count, latest_cursor, has_more}` (no request_id/timestamp). If no conversation exists yet, returns an empty list + `latest_cursor: null`.

parameters.name: after
parameters.description: Keyset cursor — a message id (preferred, from a prior latest_cursor) or an ISO-8601 timestamp. Invalid/foreign value → 422.

post.description: Post a message to the encounter's conversation (created lazily if needed). `sender_type` chooses whose identity the message is attributed to — the sender id is derived server-side (provider → assigned provider's user, else the patient), never trusted from input.

Create a prescription for the encounter and transition it to PRESCRIBED. Authorization is ROLE-based: an admin, or the encounter's assigned provider — patient/client/sales-org tokens are 403'd. post.description: Side-effect-free preclusion/validation preview for a proposed prescription — no persistence, no status change. Returns validity plus errors/warnings/checks.

Request a refill. Requires `prescription:read` plus refill authorization (admin / assigned provider / owning patient / owning client or sales-org). A plain Rx charges the card on file (product + shipping); a subscription-backed Rx routes through the subscription lane. When there is no card on file, the response indicates a checkout fallback the client must complete.

The HTTP status reflects the outcome: `charged` / `subscription` / `checkout_fallback` → 200; `payment_failed` → **402**.

post.summary: Provide missing information for a held encounter
post.description:
Submit the information a held (REQUIRES_INFORMATION) encounter is waiting on. Requires `patient:read` AND `patient:update`. Accepts `multipart/form-data` so identity photos can be uploaded. Send only the fields that were missing (all optional). The action requires the encounter to be held with NO provider attached (else 409); when every required item is satisfied it clears the hold and transitions the encounter to UNASSIGNED (re-enters auto-assign) — otherwise it stays held and returns 422 with what's still missing.

Discover exactly which fields/documents to send via `GET /me/patient/encounters/{encounterId}/requirements`.

address_zip.description: Shipping address is a hard intake gate.

bearerAuth.description:

`Accept: application/json` on every request — see the "Required Headers"
section in the API description for details.

MUST be `application/json` on every request. Without this header,
authentication failures return a 302 redirect to the web login page
instead of a JSON 401 response. The server injects this header via
middleware as a safety net, but clients should still send it explicitly.

Clinician sections and evidence_score are null for audience=patient.

the token holds peptide:clinical:read.

field — `weight_lbs` for `weight`, `systolic`+`diastolic` for
`blood_pressure`, `glucose_mgdl` for `glucose`, etc. The
type-specific endpoints (e.g. `/me/patient/vitals/weight`) provide
stricter, per-type schemas.

fasting.description: Glucose only — was the reading taken fasting?

wholesale_price.description:
Token-gated. Present only when caller is sales-org / client / admin.
Sales-org overrides applied when `wholesale_override=true` on
`sales_organization_products`.

Org-set patient-facing price (e.g. promo / member rate). Present
only when sales-org override row defines a non-zero value.

this field returns the integer enum value (was the label). Use

When true, this is a no-product quick-consult type (Async/Chat/
Voice/Video). It is the ONLY case in which a unified intake may be
submitted WITHOUT a product/package/plan selection.

requires_verification.description: Whether one-time-code re-verification is required at join on an untrusted device.

no_show_at.description: When the visit was marked a no-show (still reschedulable).

rescheduled_at.description: When the visit was last rescheduled.

reschedule_count.description: Number of times the visit has been rescheduled.

product_total.description: Sum of order line totals before discounts and shipping.

gateway_payment_profile_id.description: Existing CIM payment profile (for link mode)

Subscription.description: The enriched subscription resource (#5 B-6). Carries the billing plan, resolved billing mode, coupon summary, billing-ownership flags, per-sub renewal_mode / term_prepaid, a redacted sticky-merchant summary (NO credentials), and the next pending checkpoint forecast. Every money field is a decimal STRING.

package_plan_id.description: The billing plan this subscription enrolled on (#5 B-6).

billing_mode.description: Resolved commercial billing mode, from the plan (else package). Lowercased enum name, not the integer backing value.

initial_order_id.description: The order that seeded this subscription (rebill line source when present).

coupon_code.description: Applied coupon code (#5 B-6), or null.

coupon_is_recurring.description: Whether the coupon discount carries forward to every cycle (vs one-time).

coupon_discount_amount.description: Frozen per-cycle coupon discount (decimal string, "0.00" when none).

rebill_managed_externally.description: A 3rd party owns recurring billing + follow-up creation.

auto_process_suppressed.description: The engine schedules but never auto-charges/ships/reassesses this sub.

external_billing_domain.description: The external system that bills this sub (required when billed externally).

renewal_mode.description: Per-sub renewal driving mode (#5). null = defer to the org scope (RebillAutomationMode, default consent-required). 'external' aliases billing_owner=external.

term_prepaid.description: The term was paid up front; PRX never re-collects on in-term refills (#5 B-5).

merchant_account_id.description: Sticky merchant the vaulted card lives on (#5 B-6). No credentials.

payment_method_id.description: The sticky vaulted payment method used for rebills.

next_checkpoint.description: The next PENDING checkpoint forecast, or null.

subscription_items.description: Line specs (product/qty/price) used to seed rebill orders when no initial order.

CreateSubscriptionRequest.description: Enroll a subscription. Requires permission `subscription-payment-manage`; the caller must be able to see the target chart (attribution is derived from the chart's owning client/sales-org, never from a caller field). Send an `Idempotency-Key` header to make retries safe (see the POST /subscriptions endpoint). The product may be given by package_plan_id (preferred — implies its package + product type), product_identifier (slug/name/SKU), package_id, or product_type_id.

package_plan_id.description: #5 B-1 — the billing plan. Implies its package + product type and provides the rebill line source, so PRX-billed subs created via API can actually be rebilled.

client_id.description: Admin-only override; otherwise derived from the chart.

sales_organization_id.description: Admin-only override; otherwise derived from the chart.

subscription_items.description: Optional line specs (product/qty/price). Used as the rebill line source when no initial order exists (waterfall: initial order → subscription_items → plan lines).

billing_owner.description: Who owns the recurring charge + follow-up creation. prescribe_rx (default) = PRX rebills the vaulted card on schedule. external = the 3rd party bills on its own system; the sub is flagged EXTERNAL + auto-process-suppressed (the engine schedules for forecasting but never auto-charges/ships/reassesses). Requires external_billing_domain.

renewal_mode.description: #5 — per-sub renewal driving mode, consulted BEFORE the org scope. prompted = patient consent required each rebill; auto = rebill automatically; external ALIASES billing_owner=external. Omit to defer to the org default.

term_prepaid.description: #5 B-5 — the term was paid up front. PRX suppresses in-term re-collection on refills.

UnifiedIntakeRequest.description:
Single-call payload that creates (or matches) a patient chart, opens
an encounter, persists intake answers, optionally records consents
and a payment, optionally schedules an appointment, and optionally
attaches identification + uploaded documents.

**Encounter type resolution** (one of, priority id > slug > name):
`encounter_type_id` | `encounter_type_slug` | `encounter_type_name`.

**Tenant resolution**: `client_id`/`client_number` and
`sales_org_id`/`sales_org_number`. Falls back to the authenticated
token's tenant when omitted.

**Shipping address is REQUIRED** (as of 2026-07-14, Encounter Intake
Safeguards). Shipping is the compliance anchor — it drives
provider-license-state and FC-licensed-state validation — so every
intake MUST carry a shipping address with `street`, `city`, `state`,
`zip` (`street2`/apt optional). Provide it as EITHER
`patient.shipping_address` OR the generic `patient.address`. Billing is
derived from shipping unless you send a distinct `patient.billing_address`.
Missing/incomplete shipping → `422` with per-field errors.

**Quick-consult exception:** for a quick-consult type
(`is_quick_consult: true`, nothing to ship) only the shipping **state**
is required (for provider-license matching) — not the full street/zip.
For a returning patient, a shipping address already on file satisfies
this requirement.

**Address shapes** (shipping required, billing optional): one of —
  1. `patient.address` (legacy single — used as both shipping + billing)
  2. `patient.shipping_address` + `patient.billing_address` (distinct)
  3. `patient.shipping_address` + `patient.billing_same_as_shipping=true`

**`patient.phone` is REQUIRED.**

**Catalog selection**: prefer the nested `products[]`/`packages[]`
shape. The legacy flat `product_ids[]`/`package_id` shape is still
accepted for backward compat with embed forms. A product, package, or
plan selection is **REQUIRED unless the encounter type is a quick
consult** (`is_quick_consult: true` — see
`GET /telehealth/encounter-types`). Non-quick-consult intake with no
catalog selection → `422`.

**Duplicate handling**: a re-POST for the same patient + encounter type
within 20 days is treated as a resubmission and merged ADDITIVELY (fills
blanks only). If the re-POST CHANGES an already-populated field
(corrected phone / name), the request is rejected with `409` — send the
correction to `PATCH /patients/{id}` (demographics),
`PATCH /encounters/{id}` (visit), or `PATCH /encounters/{id}/answers`
(screening) instead of re-POSTing the intake.

is_sandbox.description:
Flags the encounter (and any resulting order) as `is_sandbox=true`.
Sandbox flow:
  - skips provider auto-assignment (capacity preserved)
  - skips fulfillment dispatch (carriers / pharmacies not hit)
  - excludes the order from commission + billing-statement reports
The flag is also auto-set when the patient's first or last name
matches `/\btest(ing|er)?\b/i` (e.g. "Test Patient", "John Tester").
Explicit payload value wins over name detection.

date_of_birth.description: ISO date, must be before today.

answers.description:
Intake answers keyed by field slug from
`GET /telehealth/encounter-types/{id}/schema`. Value formats
vary by field type:
  - text → string
  - number → number
  - yes_no → "Yes" | "No"
  - select → option value string
  - multiselect → string[]
  - toggle → boolean
  - height → {"feet":5,"inches":10}
  - blood_pressure → {"systolic":120,"diastolic":80}
`ApiIntakeDependencyValidator` runs after this validation pass to
enforce conditional requireds (e.g., follow-up answers required
when a parent answer is "Yes").

products.description:
Ordered product lines. Each item must specify **EXACTLY ONE**
identifier (multiple → 422; missing all → 422). The identifier you
choose sets how specific the order is — from a fixed SKU down to a
broad class the provider narrows at prescribe-time:

| Identifier | Selects | Who picks the final SKU |
|---|---|---|
| `product_id` | one exact SKU (UUID) | already fixed |
| `product_number` | one exact SKU (`PROD-XXXXX`) | already fixed |
| `product_type_id` | a medication **type** (e.g. Tirzepatide) | provider, from SKUs of that type |
| `product_type_slug` | same, by slug (e.g. `tirzepatide`) | provider, from SKUs of that type |
| `product_class_id` | a medication **class** (broadest — one level above type) | provider, from any type in the class |
| `product_class_slug` | same, by slug | provider, from any type in the class |

Generic identifiers (`product_type_*` / `product_class_*`) create an
`is_generic_reference` line with `product_id = null`; the provider's
prescribing panel renders it as "medication → pick dose → pick
eligible SKU". Use these when you want the provider to choose the
concentration/SKU (e.g. titration, or when the patient bought "a GLP-1"
rather than a specific vial). This mirrors the embed form's
PackageItem `is_generic_reference` semantics.

**Quantity handling — `quantity` and `term_months` are two
INDEPENDENT axes; they do NOT multiply:**
  - `quantity` = the discrete number of **units purchased** (1–99).
    This is what the patient paid for and the default quantity the
    provider sees on the line. Send the real count — ordering 3 units
    must send `quantity: 3` (a common integration bug is sending the
    type/SKU but omitting quantity, so the patient is billed for 3 but
    only 1 unit is prescribed/shipped).
  - `term_months` = the intended **supply duration in months** (1–24)
    for an ad-hoc, no-package multi-month order. It sets the line's
    `requested_months`; it does not change how many units are ordered.
  - Both default to `1`. For `packages[]`, `quantity` scales the whole
    package (ordering 2× a package doubles every line in it); package
    term/duration comes from the package's plan, not `term_months`.

product_type_id.description: Generic medication TYPE — provider selects the concrete SKU/concentration of this type at prescribe-time.

product_class_id.description: Generic medication CLASS (broadest) — provider selects any product of any type within this class at prescribe-time.

dose_product_id.description: Optional — pre-select a specific dose→product binding.

quantity.description: Discrete units purchased (NOT units-per-month). Defaults to 1.

term_months.description: Intended supply duration in months for ad-hoc (no-package) multi-month orders. Independent of quantity. Defaults to 1.

snapshot_price.description: Optional — price shown to the patient at selection, for reconciliation.

notes.description: Optional free-text note carried to the prescribing panel.

packages.description:
Packages. Each item must specify EXACTLY ONE of `package_id` |
`package_number`. Optional `plan_id` selects a specific
subscription term (one of the package's plans).

metadata.description: Opaque pass-through metadata (affiliate/click IDs, attribution tags, UTM, etc.). Persisted to `encounters.metadata`, surfaced on the admin + sales-org encounter views, returned by `GET /encounters/{id}` (`data.metadata`), and copied onto the resulting order (`orders.metadata`, returned by the order API) so `order.paid` consumers can read it directly. Example: { "ef_transaction_id": "..." }.

external_reference.description: Optional single opaque reference string (alternative to metadata). Persisted on the encounter and returned by `GET /encounters/{id}`.

fulfillment_preferences.description:
Optional pass-through to the encounter + per-product overrides.
Nulls inherit FC defaults / vendor defaults. See
`docs/dev/FC_OVERRIDES_ARCHITECTURE.md` §3 for the resolution chain.

appointment.description: Optional. When present, the time is mapped ONTO the encounter (not a detached appointment row): it sets `scheduled_at`, assigns the provider (→ `SCHEDULED`), and provisions the video room + persistent join link (returned as `video_room` in the response). This is booking flow (1) — book inline at intake. Booking flow (2) is: create the encounter without this block, `GET /scheduling/availability/slots`, then `POST /encounters/{id}/schedule`.

provider_profile_id.description: Required within this block. (To let the platform auto-assign an eligible provider for a slot, use the encounter-first flow via `POST /encounters/{id}/schedule`, where the provider is optional.)

scheduled_start.description: Must be in the future. Stored in UTC.

patient_timezone.description: IANA timezone used to interpret a naive `scheduled_start`.

identification.description:
Required by some encounter types (controlled-substance Rx,
pharmacy-compliance audits) and stored on the patient chart.

documents.description:
Up to 20 files per intake, max 10MB each. Each entry needs:
  - `type` — document category
  - `filename` — including extension
  - either `file_base64` (preferred) OR `url` (HTTPS only,
    fetched server-side)
Files persist as PatientDocument rows linked to both the chart
and the encounter, mirroring the embed wizard's upload path.
MIME is sniffed server-side; mismatched declared `mime_type` →
422.

file_base64.description: Base64-encoded file bytes — required if `url` not provided.

url.description: HTTPS URL fetched server-side. Required if `file_base64` not provided.

UnifiedIntakePaymentBlock.description:
Payment intent. Choose ONE of five modes:

| mode                 | When to use                                        | PRX runs gateway? |
|----------------------|----------------------------------------------------|-------------------|
| `authorize`          | Embed flow only — PRX is merchant of record.       | yes (pre-auth)    |
| `reference_preauth`  | You ran a pre-auth on your gateway; vault + record.| no                |
| `reference_captured` | You already ran a full sale; record-only audit.    | no                |
| `prepaid`            | Out-of-band billing already settled.               | no                |
| `patient_review`     | Defer payment to a downstream patient portal flow. | no                |

**Sales-org / client tokens cannot use `authorize`** — see the token
guard in the auth section. Use `reference_captured` or
`patient_review` from API integrations.

For `reference_preauth` / `reference_captured`, `gateway` accepts any
free-form string — the integrator's gateway name is recorded for
audit, but PRX never calls back to it.

## Capture timing & flow (per mode)

Payment does not always settle at intake. What happens, and WHEN, depends
on the mode and (for auth-only workflows) on the encounter's
`OrderWorkflowType`:

- **`authorize` (embed only):** PRX pre-authorizes at checkout, then captures
  per the workflow — `provider_direct`/`staged` capture the **full authorized
  amount when the provider finalizes the prescription**
  (`encounter.prescribed`); `patient_review` captures the base at prescribe
  and defers provider-added extras to the patient portal (see below).
- **`reference_preauth`:** you already hold the funds. With
  `capture_responsibility=on_prescribe`, PRX captures the hold on
  `encounter.prescribed` — **subscribe to the `encounter.prescribed` webhook
  if instead YOU capture**, that is your capture signal. With the default
  `third_party`, PRX never captures; you own capture + liability, and PRX
  ships only once you report funds collected.
- **`reference_captured`:** funds already settled; recorded for audit only.
- **`prepaid`:** out-of-band billing already settled; no PRX transaction.
- **`patient_review`:** no charge at intake. The provider prescribes, the base
  is settled, and any **provider-ADDED** item is offered to the patient for a
  separate, consented charge via the patient-approval API
  (`GET/POST /me/patient/approvals*`). Accepting fires `approval.accepted`;
  declining fires `approval.declined` (a declined item never ships).

> **If PRX does NOT capture (you do):** the outbound webhook to key your own
> capture on is **`encounter.prescribed`**. Correlate by the
> `external_order_id` you passed at intake, echoed on every order/encounter
> event. Deliver webhooks to your subscription URL configured under
> `POST /api/v1/webhooks` on `https://prescribe-rx.com`. Full contract +
> worked examples: the Payment Integrator Webhook Guide.

An `authorization` is a **ceiling** — PRX captures at most the authorized
amount, never more. A provider-added item that exceeds the hold is collected
as a **separate** patient-consented charge (never from the base hold).

## What to send (the nonce never crosses to PRX)

A single-use checkout nonce is never sent to PRX and is never useful to it —
exchange it for a durable vault/customer profile on your gateway at checkout
and send those ids. `card_token` is hard-validated to be a durable profile
(a recognizable nonce shape — Accept.js opaque data, Square `cnon:`, Stripe
`tok_` — is rejected 422).

| operation | needs |
|---|---|
| **Base capture** (on_prescribe) | `merchant_account_id` + the auth's `gateway_transaction_id` + amount — **no card_token, no card data**. The gateway references the original auth (e.g. Auth.Net `priorAuthCaptureTransaction` by refTransId). |
| **Delta charge** (patient accepts a provider-added item) | a stored PaymentMethod = the durable vault profile (`card_token`) + merchant. |
| **Rebill / re-auth** (subscription, or hold expiring in review) | the durable vault profile. |

> Capture alone does not need `card_token` — but **still send it**. Because a
> ceiling auth can never be stretched to cover an add-on (the over-capture
> guard rejects `amount > authorized`), the delta is a fresh charge that needs
> its own instrument: without a vaulted profile the FIRST provider-added item
> dead-ends (the accept endpoint returns 402 "No card on file"), and
> subscription rebills / re-auth-on-expiry have nothing to charge.

## Reconciling captures (two independent sources)

When PRX captures an Rx hold, the gateway (Auth.Net/Stripe) fires its own
capture webhook AND PRX fires `order.paid`. Treat them as two independent
sources: the **gateway webhook is authoritative for "money moved"**; the
**PRX webhook says "why, and against which order."** To let you mate them
with no dependency on PRX getting a field right, `order.placed` /
`order.paid` / `order.status_changed` / `order.cancelled` now carry
**`encounter_id`** and **`gateway_transaction_id`** (plus your
`external_order_id`) — the gateway id is the same one on the gateway's own
capture webhook. Disagreement between the two sources should be an alert.
Don't rely on webhooks alone: `GET /orders/{id}/transactions` backstops a
daily sweep over anything stuck `authorized`.

gateway.description:
For `mode=authorize`, must be one of `authorize_net | stripe | nmi | square`
(PRX-supported gateways). Other modes accept any string.

merchant_account_id.description:
**Optional but important — this is what links an externally-processed
charge to a PrescribeRx merchant so future billing runs on-system.**

For `reference_preauth` / `reference_captured`: the charge already ran on
YOUR gateway, outside PrescribeRx. Pass the UUID of the merchant account
you configured in PrescribeRx for that same gateway and PRX will:
  1. stamp this transaction with that `merchant_account_id` (instead of
     leaving it null / audit-only), and
  2. — together with a `card_token` (see below) — vault a **rechargeable**
     card on that merchant, so future subscription rebills, refills,
     deferred captures, and refunds can be processed **on-system**.

**PREREQUISITE (do this in PrescribeRx first):** as a sales org you must
add the merchant account under **Settings → Payments → Merchant Accounts**
with the gateway credentials for the same gateway you charged on. Without a
matching, active merchant account, this field cannot resolve and the
transaction is recorded with a null merchant (audit-only, NOT rechargeable).

**Validation:** the merchant's `gateway_provider` must equal `gateway`, the
account must be `is_active`, and it must belong to the intake's sales org
(cross-tenant guard). On mismatch PRX logs the reason
(`explicit merchant gateway mismatch` / `not owned by intake org`) and falls
back to null rather than charging on the wrong account.

Omit for `mode=authorize` (PRX routes its own merchant) and for
`prepaid` / `patient_review` (no transaction recorded).

workflow.description:
Optional override for `OrderWorkflowType`. When omitted,
`CheckoutWorkflowService::resolveWorkflow()` picks based on embed
config + encounter type.

card_token.description:
**The durable, gateway-side vault references for the card you charged —
supplying this (WITH a valid `merchant_account_id`) is what makes the
card RECHARGEABLE on-system.** PRX stores it as a local, rechargeable
PaymentMethod on your merchant so the recurring engine / staff can bill
future rebills, refills, and refunds without you re-sending card data.

If you send `card_metadata` only (brand/last4/exp) and NO `card_token`,
PRX stores a **display-only** receipt card — visible on the chart but NOT
chargeable. Send `card_token` whenever you want future on-system billing.

The shape is gateway-specific — send the durable profile ids your gateway
returns from its vault/customer API (NOT a one-time nonce):
  - **stripe:** `{ "customer_id": "cus_…", "payment_method_id": "pm_…" }`
  - **authorize_net:** `{ "customer_profile_id": "…", "payment_profile_id": "…" }`
  - **nmi:** `{ "customer_vault_id": "…" }`
  - **square:** `{ "customer_id": "…", "card_id": "…" }`

The merchant's gateway must match these refs (it's the account that owns
the vaulted card) — PRX hard-validates the gateway match and rejects a
rechargeable vault on a mismatched merchant (degrading to display-only
rather than storing an uncharg­eable token).

card_metadata.description:
Brand / last4 / expiry for DISPLAY on the patient chart. Sufficient on its
own only for a display-only card; pair with `card_token` for a rechargeable
one. Required when `mode=reference_captured` and you want any stored card.

capture_responsibility.description:
**Who captures a `reference_preauth` hold.** (Also accepted inside
`pre_auth.capture_responsibility`.)

- `third_party` — **default.** YOU capture on your own gateway. PRX
  never touches the hold; it is your liability regardless. PRX will not
  hold fulfillment waiting on a hold it does not own, and will not link
  it to the order (so the order routes on its own terms — see the flow
  notes above).
- `on_prescribe` — PRX captures the hold when the provider **finalizes
  the prescription** (`encounter.prescribed`). The hold is then treated
  as PRX-owned: linked to the order, held at the ship-gate until
  captured, and captured by the prescribe-time capture listener. Vault a
  rechargeable card (`card_token` + `merchant_account_id`) so PRX can act
  on it.
- `already_captured` — implied by `mode=reference_captured`; nothing left
  to capture.

Ignored for `authorize` / `prepaid` / `patient_review`.

WebhookEnvelope.description:
Standard delivery body. Every webhook POST has this envelope; the
`data` block varies per event slug — see the per-event payload
schemas (`WebhookEncounterCreatedData`, `WebhookOrderPlacedData`, etc.).

**Headers on every delivery:**
- `X-PrescribeRx-Signature: sha256=<hex>` — HMAC-SHA256 of the raw
  request body using your subscription's signing secret.
- `X-Webhook-ID` — UUID; use as your idempotency key.
- `X-Webhook-Event` — the event slug.
- `X-Webhook-Timestamp` — ISO-8601 timestamp matching `timestamp`.
- `User-Agent: PrescribeRx-Webhook/1.0`.

**Order correlation (`external_order_id`):** when the originating order
entered through the External Telehealth Orders API, the integrator's own
`external_order_id` is echoed in the `data` block so you can correlate a
webhook back to the order YOU placed without holding our id map. It is
present on every event that traces to such an order — order/fulfillment
events directly, and encounter/subscription/refill/reassessment/lab/
prescription/appointment events via their originating order. The field is
simply absent (not null) for events whose order was created internally
(admin UI, embed checkout, etc.) or that have no originating order.

timestamp.description: ISO-8601 timestamp the event was emitted.

webhook_id.description:
Unique per delivery (NOT per event — retries reuse the same id).
Use as your idempotency key.

data.description:
Event-specific payload. Shape depends on the `event` slug —
consult the per-slug schema. All payloads are non-PHI: identifiers,
status fields, timestamps. No clinical content.

ChatBranding.description:
Per-agent branding payload. All fields optional. Missing keys
fall back to widget defaults (neutral blue, system font, no
logo). Edits flow live to mounted widgets on the next page
load — no sales-org redeploy needed.

avatar_url.description: 32×32 round image in the chat header. Square images render best.

logo_url.description:
Optional wider rectangular brand mark (up to 160×32). When
set, replaces the round avatar and the header slot adopts
the `prxc-has-logo` class.

color.description:
Primary brand color. Hex, leading `#` recommended.
Drives header background, user message bubbles, send
button, and the suggestion-card "Add to cart" button.
Surfaced as the `--prxc-brand` CSS variable.

secondary_color.description:
Accent color. Drives suggestion-card price text and a 3px
left border on bot messages. Falls back to `color` when
unset. Surfaced as the `--prxc-brand-secondary` CSS variable.

font_family.description:
CSS `font-family` stack applied to the entire widget root.
**The host page is responsible for loading any web fonts**
via `@font-face` or `<link>` — the widget does not.

custom_css.description:
Raw CSS injected into the host page as a separate
`<style id="prxc-custom-styles">` tag. **Admins are
responsible for scoping selectors with `.prxc-root`** so
rules don't leak onto the rest of the host site. Same
trust model as `system_prompt_overrides` (admin-only).

opening_message.description: First chat bubble shown to the visitor when the panel opens.
opening_message.example: Hi! What are you looking to address today?

max_conversation_turns.description: Soft cap. The widget surfaces a "Start over" banner once exceeded.

message.description: Visitor's message for this turn. Plain text — no markdown processing.

conversation_id.description:
UUID returned by the previous turn. Pass `null` (or omit)
on the first turn — the response carries the new id.
**Cross-tenant safe:** if the id belongs to a different
agent, the server starts a fresh conversation rather than
reading the foreign thread.

visitor_fingerprint.description:
Anonymous visitor token persisted by the widget in
`localStorage` under `__prxChatFp`. Used for
repeat-visitor analytics (Phase 5/6). Never PHI.

ChatProductSuggestion.description:
One product card the model recommended. The `product_id` is
guaranteed to be inside the agent's strict allowed-set
(catalog post-filter — hallucinated ids are dropped before
the response leaves the controller).

product_id.description: Canonical product UUID. Hand to `PrescribeRx.addProduct(id)` if running the embed bridge, or to your custom cart.

price.description: Sales-org retail price, already org-cascaded by `PricingService`.

reason.description: One-sentence justification the model produced for this customer's specific message.
reason.example: Supports the energy + athletic-recovery goal you mentioned.

conversation_id.description: Pass back on every subsequent turn for context continuity.

turn_count.description: How many turns the conversation has used. Compared to `max_conversation_turns` on the init response.

conversation_complete.description:
`true` once the turn cap is hit. The widget disables the
input and renders a "Start over" banner. New turns return
HTTP 410 with the same flag.

reply.description: Free-text assistant reply, ≤ 4 sentences (model-side rule). Always ends with the disclaimer "Not medical advice — a licensed provider reviews everything during intake."

suggestions.description: 0 to `max_suggestions_per_response` cards. Empty when the model is still gathering info.

npi.description: 10-digit NPI. Dashes/whitespace allowed; stripped on save.

message.example: Provider already exists at this client.

signed_at.description: ISO 8601 timestamp when your e-Rx system signed the PDF.
